messages.subject: multiple within-population variance estimates
messages.body_plain:
For a nested provenance/progeny design, I did not find the syntax to estimate one family variance (or genetic variance using pedigree) for each population (and not one single mean within-population variance). Sorry I probably missed something.
Thank you for helping,
best regards,
François

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] multiple within-population variance estimates
messages.body_plain:
Indeed, there is no straightforward specification of this model.

You can use the `generic` model to manually specify a genetic component for each population.
You need to manipulate the incidence matrices in order to link each observation with the corresponding effect.
A similar setup is used in the vignette Additive Genetic Models in Mixed Populations. <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/wiki/Additive-Genetic-Models-in-Mixed-Populations.pdf>

Let me know if this works for your situation.
Also, I'd welcome suggestions regarding the syntax supporting this type of models.

Best
        ƒacu.-

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the answer, the syntax is rather logical and seems to be very generic, but quite complex for a simple (and I guess current) situation as I explained.

for a basic estimate of a progeny variance for each population (without a pedigree, actually it comes to consider the populations as fixed and estimate a random effect within each level), could there be someting similar to lme syntax, like:  random = ~ pop|desc  ?
this would already allow to compare a model with a single progeny variance estimate, with a model having several progeny variances.
=> am I correct?

Then if we come to estimate the additive variance within each population, I see 2 situations:

1) we are dealing just with independent populations therefore, as you say in your vignette, there is nothing to learn for one population from the other, then we can run a classical model with pedigree independently in as many sub-datasets as populations
=> am I correct?

2) we are dealing with a mixture, e.g. diallel based on parents from multiple populations, then you procedure is clear enough

messages.subject: Error msg when running a model with competition
messages.subject_clean: Error msg when running a model with competition
messages.body_plain:
I try to integrate competition in the model, but when I run the following command I receive an error message:

res.comp<-remlf90(fixed=d99~1,
                 random=~1,
                 genetic=list(model='competition',pedigree=ped,id="arbre",
                              coord = data[, c('Y', 'X')],
                              competition_decay = 1,
                              pec = list(present = TRUE)),
                 spatial=list(model="AR",coord=data[,c("Y","X")]),
                 data=data)

> Erreur : sum(idx <- !is.na <http://is.na>(conv)) == 1 n'est pas TRUE

=> is it an error in the syntax ? or a pb with the data ? or a pb with the design in the field ?

Note: the same syntax without competition,runs correctly
res.nocomp<-remlf90(fixed=d99~1,
                 random=~1,
                 genetic=list(model='add_animal',pedigree=ped,id="arbre"),
                 spatial=list(model="AR",coord=data[,c("Y","X")]),
                 data=data)

Thank's for the hotline !

messages.body_plain:

(sorry I must have missed this point in the tutorial)

messages.subject_clean: [breedR] Re: Error msg when running a model with competition
messages.body_plain:
Hi! thanks for reporting.

Indeed, the issue was that competition models were assumed not to be run with 'ai'.
However this brings into the open other weaknesses in the interface.
I have filed a couple of new issues as a result from this: https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/issues/67

ƒacu.-
